cases.oracle: Fresh world (terrain rows y<4 grass, y<10 dirt, y<18 stone, else wood) with stone at (5,5): click 1 leaves the stone present, records cell damage hits=1 and draws crack overlay stage 1 as a pure function of (x, y, stage); click 2 leaves it present with hits=2 and crack stage 2 visually distinct from stage 1, with damage accumulating on cell-entry edges only (no extra hits from pointermove inside the same cell); click 3 reaches hardness 3, removes the stone (cell becomes empty), clears its damage-map entry, increments the stone (type 3) inventory by exactly 1, and the canvas HUD shows the incremented count; wood (type 4) behaves identically at hardness 3 while grass and dirt stay hardness 1 in the registry.

Fresh world with grass at (10,10): a single click removes the grass (cell empty), increments the grass (type 1) inventory by exactly 1, and leaves no damage-map entry and no crack overlay for that cell; dirt (type 2) is likewise removed on the first click (hardness 1).

With stone inventory >= 1 after mining, placing stone from the palette onto an empty cell decrements stone inventory by exactly 1 and the cell becomes stone; with stone inventory exactly 0 a placement attempt is refused before any mutation: the cell stays empty, stone inventory stays 0, and the palette entry for that type renders greyed out at zero; counters remain non-negative integers over types 1..4 and never go negative.

After mining and placing so that both world cells and inventory changed, the save at the single localStorage key (minicraft-grid-v1) is one atomic blob {version:2, cells, inventory} with inventory as non-negative integers over keys 1..4; a reload (fresh boot reading the same key) restores world cells and inventory deep-equal to the pre-reload state while the transient damage map resets to empty; a stored v1 blob {version, cells} migrates on load with inventory defaulted to zero for every type; with empty localStorage the first boot yields the default terrain world and an all-zero inventory.

cleanup.environment: Run from the repo root with the Node >= 18 built-in test runner; no browser, dev server or network access required; the run must leave no environment mutation.
cleanup.data: The logic suite injects an in-memory storage stub for the save key; no real browser localStorage, world blob or project file is written, and a completed run leaves no data artifacts.
